title: Treasury
subtitle: Bank accounts, statements, bank charges and reconciliation
summary: Treasury links each bank account to its GL cash account, imports bank statements (CSV or Excel), posts bank charges and interest straight from statement lines, and reconciles statement lines to GL lines with auto-match and manual matching until the difference is zero.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The book balance is the GL balance of the bank's cash account (1100), read through GlBalanceReader. The bank's own view arrives as statement lines.
Auto-match pairs statement lines with GL lines of the same amount within MATCH_WINDOW_DAYS. What is left is matched by hand or explained (a bank charge or interest is posted straight from the line).
A reconciliation can only be completed with every line matched and no difference; after that it is locked.

sections.title: Treasury explained in plain English
sections.intro: A profitable business can still run out of cash. Treasury is where accountants check that the bank and the company’s own books tell a consistent story.
items: General Ledger (GL) is what the company recorded. The bank statement is what the bank recorded. These are independent records that may temporarily disagree.
Accounts Receivable (AR) brings money in when customers settle invoices; Accounts Payable (AP) pays suppliers. Treasury confirms whether those cash movements actually reached or left the bank.
A bank transaction is an imported statement line—an actual bank debit or credit. It is not automatically proof of the correct GL posting.
A reconciliation is a dated comparison. Reconciliation lines document which bank transactions match which GL journal lines; a nullable journal-line reference permits unresolved matches.
A completed reconciliation is a controlled financial assertion, not just a green label. The application must check differences, unmatched items, and authorization before closing it.

sections.title: From statement upload to completed reconciliation
items: 1. Identify the bank account: bank account, currency, owning legal entity, and linked GL cash account.
2. Import bank statement: validate format, dates, amount signs, duplicates, and bank-reference uniqueness.
3. Create reconciliation: select the statement date and record opening and closing balances.
4. Auto-match: use reliable references, amounts, dates, and other evidence to associate bank lines with GL journal lines.
5. Review unmatched lines: investigate timing differences, missing or duplicate postings, charges, and interest.
6. Post corrections safely: authorized accounting events or GL journals should record legitimate missing bank fees and interest.
7. Complete only when validated: confirm required matches, balance differences and policy controls, then close the reconciliation.
